source.title: A Hessian Based Complexity Measure for Deep Networks
source.authors: Hamid Javadi; Randall Balestriero; Richard Baraniuk

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper. Its title differs from the catalog title: the text is “Implicit Rugosity Regularization via Data Augmentation.”
record.tranche_reason: The paper experimentally tests whether data augmentation and explicit rugosity regularization affect measured complexity and test accuracy, bearing on whether lower rugosity tracks a smaller generalization gap. It does not directly test most listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: Rows capture reported measurements of rugosity and test accuracy under data augmentation and explicit rugosity regularization. The paper's introductory statement that networks can fit pure noise cites Zhang et al.; it is not this study's own result. Figure 2 reports curve values only in plots, so those values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study measures input-space tangent-Hessian rugosity, not V7's tolerance to magnitude-scaled weight perturbations. Its augmentation and rugosity-penalty experiments do not test any listed version. Random-label fitting and dropout are cited background, without corresponding experiments.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate but needs the architecture qualification: augmentation clearly reduces measured rugosity for ResNets, while converged CNN results are mixed. Explicit rugosity penalties reduce rugosity without generally improving test accuracy; increasing the penalty can reduce test accuracy despite zero training error. The authors also explain limitations of derivative-based complexity measures.
record.recipe_differences: Studies data augmentation as an implicit rugosity regularizer and adds a Hessian-based rugosity penalty; it does not test the listed original interventions or measures directly.
record.method_sensitivity: Effects vary by architecture (CNN versus ResNet), dataset, and whether rugosity is measured on training or test data; explicit-penalty outcomes vary with λ.

fits_no_version.finding: Augmentation lowers squared input-space rugosity across the listed ResNets, but converged CNN rugosity changes are mixed. ResNet test accuracy is unchanged on MNIST and increases on SVHN, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data augmentation can reduce input-space tangent-Hessian rugosity, with effects depending on architecture and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Explicit rugosity regularization lowers rugosity without test-accuracy gains; the authors state that increasing its weight lowers test accuracy despite zero training error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reducing input-space rugosity through an explicit penalty need not improve classification generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5 shows that scaling classification outputs can make derivative-based rugosity arbitrarily small while preserving predicted labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unnormalized derivative-based rugosity alone cannot determine classification generalization.

record.problems: Table 1 omits some measurements due to time constraints. Figure 2 reports plotted curves without textual numeric values. No uncertainty estimates are provided. Explicit rugosity regularization does not generally improve test accuracy, and the authors discuss limitations of complexity measures based on derivatives.
record.rows_left_out: None. The table results and separate plotted outcomes for four λ values and four plotted measures were retained; Figure 2 exact values are unavailable and recorded as figure only.

untested.parts: No own experiment comparing random-label fitting and held-out performance with natural-label training.
No width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
No fully connected comparator; both CNN and ResNet architectures use convolutions.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison or tuning comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout intervention or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.

No magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, corresponding sharpness/generalization-gap ranking, or comparison against norm- and margin-based measures. Input-space Hessian rugosity is a different construct.
No identification or removal of memorized training examples.

record.verdict_notes: All states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, not judgments that the reported numerical differences are unreadable. Table 1 values match the extraction, but its rugosity columns are squared quantities. Remove all three proposed V7 verdicts: neither the favorable augmentation results nor the unfavorable explicit-penalty results establish anything about magnitude-aware weight sharpness.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label generalization comparison.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.

Tests data augmentation and explicit rugosity penalties as interventions on rugosity and test accuracy; does not compare magnitude-aware sharpness or norm- and margin-based measures, nor establish that a magnitude-aware perturbation measure ranks train-test gaps.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ResNet comparisons in Table 1 across MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR10 and CIFAR100
reader_labels.reason: Data augmentation reduced measured training and test rugosity for each listed ResNet setting; associated test accuracy was unchanged on MNIST and higher on SVHN, CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 (R9–R22).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CNN comparisons in Table 1 across MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR10 and CIFAR100
reader_labels.reason: The rugosity change with augmentation was mixed: training rugosity barely changed or rose, MNIST test rugosity rose, and CIFAR10 rugosity rose on both sets (R1–R8).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The text states that increasing λ lowered test accuracy despite zero training error, so reducing rugosity alone did not generally improve test accuracy (R23–R38).
